column1: # *** CASA 229 OF CALLE SARANDI, MONTEVIDEO, IN THE PADRON OF 1850. ***
# 12 October 2026. Found while answering a two-hour-old errand about one missing child.
# *** TWO THINGS CAME OUT OF ONE PAGE: *** Leonarda Lerena is located, and four adults who carry this
# family's surname are named for the first time - Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela and Rosa.
# *** AND A WARNING ABOUT A NUMBER THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN USING AS A NAME. *** There are at least two
# houses numbered 229 in this padron, on different streets. data/household-229-pedro-antonio.tsv is
*** THE ERRAND IS ANSWERED: SHE IS IN THE PADRON, AT ANOTHER ADDRESS ***
column2: Montevideo, padron of 1850 (libro 264) - index ark 1:1:XMKF-FR3W, image ark 3:1:3QS7-89ZP-B99S-Z, plate read at apid TH-1961-36718-27970-97
column3: *** LEONARDA LERENA, 11, BLANCA, ORIENTAL - AT CASA 229 OF CALLE SARANDI ***
column4: An errand was raised two hours earlier asking where she was, because she is absent from her parents' house in the same padron and this archive had used that absence to date the census.
column5: *** She was never missing from the census - only from her parents' house. *** Born 20 February 1837, she is thirteen in 1850 and entered as *** eleven ***, which is ordinary. *** And the house number is a trap: *** her parents are at a casa 229 on another street entirely, and this is *** Sarandi 229 ***. *** TWO DIFFERENT HOUSES, BOTH NUMBERED 229, IN ONE PADRON *** - so 'household 229' has never been an identifier, and a file in this archive is named after it.

column1: *** AND FOUR MORE PEOPLE CARRY THE SURNAME IN THAT HOUSE ***
column2: the same page, read line by line
column3: *** ESTANISLADA, 20 | SINFORIANO, 19 | MANUELA, 60 | ROSA, 46 - every one entered as D.o, ditto, for LERENA ***
column4: This archive has documented five people held in slavery by this family, among them *** Barbara ***, named on an 1846 act as 'esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena', whose son was baptised with no surname of his own.
column5: *** THE COLUMNS SAY WHAT THE NAMES DO NOT. *** Leonarda is *** blanca, oriental. *** Estanislada is *** morena ***; Sinforiano the same; *** MANUELA, sixty years old, is entered with patria AFRICA and estado casada ***; Rosa, forty-six, oriental, casada. *** Four adults of colour bearing the holder's surname, one of them African-born, living at an address where the only white person entered is an eleven-year-old girl. *** Slavery was abolished in Uruguay in 1842, so in 1850 they are legally free and still in the house, still under the name. *** That is the same pattern as Barbara's act, eight years later and four people wider. ***

column3: *** THE CENSUS DOES NOT SAY THEY WERE ENSLAVED, AND THIS FILE DOES NOT EITHER ***
column4: The padron has no column for condition; it has colour, patria and estado, and it is the combination that speaks.
column5: *** What is established: four adults recorded with the Lerena surname by ditto, three of them morena and one born in Africa, at Sarandi 229 in 1850. *** What is inferred and *** FILED AS INFERENCE ***: that the surname reached them the way Barbara's reached her son. *** What would settle it: the parish registers for these four names at the Cordon or the Catedral, where a baptism or a burial would say 'liberta' or 'esclava de' outright *** - and the Cordon burial registers of 1839-1852 are already in this archive's hands, unread. *** They are entered as people in their own right, because no role is furniture. ***
